06 / BEYOND MUNs

THE WORLD DOES NOT STOP AT THE COMMITTEE ROOM.

Model United Nations introduced many of us to diplomacy.

But diplomacy does not begin and end in a committee room.

House of Diplomacy exists to take that conversation further — through debates, politics, culture, writing, creative work, media and collaboration.

HOUSE MASTERPIECE
HOUSE MASTERPIECE VIDEO ESSAY · HOUSE MEDIA

THE POLITICS OF MANTO

A video edit by Trigun Pathak · Kolkata, India

Manto never held office, yet his words shaped how South Asia thinks about politics. On religion, he mocked leaders who cry in public that faith is in danger, arguing, "Mazhab aisi cheez hi nahi ki khatre mein pad sake" (religion is not something that can fall in danger), and that the only real danger is to the leaders who gamble with it to serve themselves. On gender, he exposed a society that condemns the women it exploits, reminding readers, "Har aurat vaishya nahi hoti lekin har vaishya aurat hoti hai" (not every woman is a prostitute, but every prostitute is a woman). He mocked moral guardians for whom "aurat ka wujood hi fohsh hai" (a woman's very existence is obscene), and argued that without the women they shun, the streets would be "gali-kooche mardon ki ghaleez harkaat se bhare" (full of men's filthy behavior). His concern for economic justice comes through in "Main baghaawat chahta hun" (I want rebellion) against everyone who takes a person's labour but refuses to pay for it. His belief that "zabaan banaai nahi jaati, khud banti hai" (language isn't manufactured, it grows on its own) quietly rejects the politics of tying language to religious identity. Together, these lines made him a lasting conscience for debates on communal politics, gender, class, and censorship.

13 / CERTIFICATESTHE HOUSE RECOGNISES CONTRIBUTION
THE HOUSE KEEPS A RECORD

WHEN AN IDEA ENTERS THE HOUSE,
IT BECOMES PART OF ITS RECORD.

House of Diplomacy formally recognises writers, artists, researchers, editors and creators whose original work contributes to the intellectual, political, cultural and creative conversations fostered by the House.

01

CERTIFICATE OF PUBLICATION

For articles, essays, opinions, analyses and written contributions published by House of Diplomacy.

02

CERTIFICATE OF CREATIVE CONTRIBUTION

For poetry, artwork, photography, creative writing and other original creative work.

03

CERTIFICATE OF EDITORIAL CONTRIBUTION

For editorial, research, curation and publication-related contributions.

04

CERTIFICATE OF MEDIA CONTRIBUTION

For interviews, documentaries, videos and other approved media contributions.

05

CERTIFICATE OF FEATURED CONTRIBUTION

For selected works that House of Diplomacy chooses to formally feature or highlight.

18 / HOW THE HOUSE SPEAKSPRINCIPLES

FACT

Verify claims and identify sources.

PERSPECTIVE

Opinions belong to their authors.

DIALOGUE

Disagreement is welcome. Personal attacks are not.

CREDIT

Original creators are credited.

CONTEXT

Complex issues should not be reduced to misleading headlines.

RESPONSIBILITY

Submitted content may be reviewed before publication.

House of Diplomacy is a platform for discourse, not a political party or campaign organisation.
